senses.gloss: Something that stays the same while everything around it changes.
examples: Through every move and job change, music was the one *constant* in his life.
Change is the only *constant* in this industry.
Sunday dinner at her mother's is one of the few *constants* in her week.

senses.gloss: A group of related people or things that appear together.
examples: The doctor looked at the whole *constellation* of symptoms before deciding.
A *constellation* of small startups has grown up around the university.
The album brought together a *constellation* of guest singers.

senses.gloss: The general health and physical strength of a person's body.
examples: He has a strong *constitution* and shook off the flu in a day.
The climb is not for anyone with a weak *constitution*.
Her *constitution* has never been the same since the surgery.

senses.gloss: A group of words put together according to the rules of grammar.
examples: The passive *construction* makes the sentence sound stiff.
Spanish has a *construction* here that English simply lacks.
He keeps mixing up two similar *constructions*.

senses.gloss: A claim that someone puts forward in an argument.
examples: His *contention* is that the tests were never run at all.
The lawyer repeated her *contention* that the search was illegal.
That *contention* is hard to square with the data.

senses.gloss: The matching of small details from shot to shot in a film or show.
senses.ru: непрерывность (соответствие деталей в кадрах, в кино)
examples: Fans spotted a *continuity* error: his glass is full again in the next shot.
Someone on set is paid to keep track of *continuity*.
The *continuity* in the fight scene falls apart halfway through.

senses.gloss: A shortened form of two words, written with an apostrophe.
examples: "Don't" is a *contraction* of "do not."
Avoid *contractions* in a formal cover letter.
The teacher circled every *contraction* in the essay.

senses.gloss: A tightening of a muscle, especially of the womb during childbirth.
examples: Her *contractions* were five minutes apart by midnight.
The nurse timed each *contraction* and wrote it down.
A sudden *contraction* in his calf woke him up.

senses.gloss: A clear difference between two things seen side by side.
examples: The *contrast* between the two brothers could not be sharper.
In *contrast* to last winter, this one has been mild.
Her calm was a welcome *contrast* to the noise around her.

senses.gloss: Someone who gives money to a campaign, a charity, or a fund.
examples: The senator returned the money to several *contributors*.
The museum lists every *contributor* on a plaque in the lobby.
She was the campaign's largest *contributor* last year.

senses.gloss: A thing that helps to cause something, usually something bad.
examples: Smoking is a major *contributor* to heart disease.
Cars are the biggest *contributor* to the city's smog.
Poor sleep is a known *contributor* to anxiety.

senses.gloss: A person whose job is to direct aircraft or traffic, or to oversee a company's accounts.
examples: An air traffic *controller* talked the pilot down through the fog.
The company's *controller* signs off on every invoice.
*Controllers* in the tower work six-hour shifts.

senses.gloss: A device or service that makes daily life easier.
examples: The cabin has no electricity and none of the usual *conveniences*.
A dishwasher is one *convenience* she refuses to give up.
The apartment is small but has every modern *convenience*.

senses.gloss: A time that suits you.
examples: Please call me back at your earliest *convenience*.
Stop by the office at your *convenience*.
We can move the meeting to suit your *convenience*.

senses.gloss: An accepted way of doing something that most people follow.
examples: By *convention*, the bride's family sits on the left.
The novel breaks every *convention* of the detective story.
Social *conventions* about tipping vary from country to country.

senses.gloss: A change from one religion or set of beliefs to another.
examples: His *conversion* to Islam surprised his family.
The book describes her *conversion* and the quiet years that followed.
The missionaries counted a handful of *conversions* that first winter.

senses.gloss: The ability to make the parts of your body work together smoothly.
examples: Catching a ball takes hand-eye *coordination*.
The stroke left him with poor *coordination* on his left side.
Toddlers are still working on their *coordination*.

senses.gloss: The prison system and the work of running it.
examples: He spent twenty years in *corrections* before he retired.
The state department of *corrections* runs eleven facilities.
A *corrections* officer walked us through the cell block.

senses.gloss: A drop in stock prices after a long rise.
examples: Analysts called the selloff a healthy *correction*.
The market entered a *correction* in October.
A ten percent *correction* is not a crash.

senses.gloss: A long narrow strip of land or route that links two places.
examples: Traffic along the I-95 *corridor* backs up every Friday.
The state is protecting a wildlife *corridor* between the two parks.
Rents have soared all along the tech *corridor*.

senses.gloss: A young adult hired to supervise children at a summer camp.
examples: She spent three summers as a *counselor* at a camp in Maine.
Our cabin *counselor* woke us at seven every morning.
The camp is still hiring *counselors* for June.

senses.gloss: A lawyer, especially one arguing a case in court.
examples: *Counselor*, approach the bench.
Both *counselors* met with the judge in chambers.
The defendant conferred quietly with his *counselor*.

senses.gloss: Something that balances or offsets an opposing force.
examples: The courts act as a *counterweight* to the president.
Small states wanted a *counterweight* to the big ones in the Senate.
Her humor was a *counterweight* to his gloom.

senses.gloss: The protection an insurance policy gives you, and what it includes.
examples: Does your plan include dental *coverage*?
She lost her health *coverage* when the job ended.
Flood damage is not part of the *coverage*.

senses.gloss: The area in which a phone or radio signal can be received.
examples: There's no cell *coverage* past the ridge.
The carrier claims *coverage* in ninety-eight percent of the state.
We lost *coverage* somewhere in the canyon.

senses.gloss: A person whose behavior is completely shaped by some habit or force.
examples: I'm a *creature* of habit — the same breakfast every day.
He is a *creature* of the party machine and always was.
She's a *creature* of the theater, at home nowhere else.

senses.gloss: The careful analysis and judgment of literature, film, or art.
examples: She teaches film *criticism* at the university.
The essay is a classic of literary *criticism*.
He moved from reporting into art *criticism*.

senses.gloss: A move into a different genre or a wider audience, or a work that makes one.
examples: The single was her *crossover* from country to pop.
The album was a rare *crossover*, charting on both the jazz and pop lists.
The two shows did a *crossover* last season.

senses.gloss: A European soldier who fought in the medieval Crusades.
examples: The *crusaders* laid siege to the city for months.
The castle was built by *crusaders* in the twelfth century.
Many *crusaders* never made it home.

senses.gloss: A strange or rare object that people find interesting.
examples: The shop is full of old *curiosities* from the sailing days.
The machine is now just a museum *curiosity*.
He kept the two-headed coin as a *curiosity*.

senses.gloss: The state of being widely accepted or used, especially of an idea or a word.
examples: The theory has gained *currency* among younger economists.
The rumor gained *currency* after the mayor refused to comment.
That word has lost its *currency* outside academic writing.

senses.gloss: An unexpected problem or surprise that is hard to deal with.
examples: Life threw us a *curveball* in March.
The interviewer opened with a *curveball*.
Be ready for a few *curveballs* on moving day.

senses.gloss: A person or body responsible for looking after something valuable.
examples: The family served as *custodians* of the letters for a century.
The library is the *custodian* of the town's records.
He saw himself as a *custodian* of the tradition, not its owner.

senses.gloss: A person of a particular kind, especially a difficult one.
examples: The guy at the door was one tough *customer*.
She's a cool *customer* under pressure.
Their new closer is a tough *customer* in the ninth inning.
